snapshot.readinessLevel: Moderate (66) — good recovery per Garmin (sleep factor 58%, recovery 99%, HRV 100% all GOOD), but multi-week sleep history is still soft (36%) after the short-sleep stretch Aug 10-12. Oura's read this morning is stronger (readiness 82, "Good — ready to train").

change: The gray zone is still the #1 lever: over the last 30 days only 43% of running time was genuinely easy (Z1-Z2, 35.7 mi) versus 47% sitting in Z3 (129-146 bpm, 39.4 mi) and 10% truly hard. The last 14 days are similar (42% easy / 46% gray / 12% hard) — keep watching HR on easy days and back off the moment it crosses ~130.

The week of Aug 10 was essentially a full stop on running (2.9 mi, one run) right after the baby arrived Aug 9 — that's exactly the right call, not a step backward. VO2max is flat at 52-52.5 and training status now reads "Peaking" (load has dropped well below what the body's used to), but ACWR is very low (0.2) so there's zero overreach risk heading back in.

Sleep took a real hit Aug 10-12 (4.6-4.9h/night, sleep scores in the 50s) and is still only partially recovered (71 last night, 5.6h). Readiness and HRV have stayed green throughout though (Oura readiness 82 today), so the body is tolerating it fine — but this is the newborn-maintenance phase now: expect volume to be whatever happens organically for a while, in the 18-32mi/wk band.
Next week's plan is deliberately conservative — ~21 mi with an optional, Oura-gated quality day — to ease back in rather than chase the 25-27 mi weeks from before the birth.
continue: Congratulations on the new arrival (Aug 9)! Recovery markers (Oura readiness 82, HRV 51-54ms balanced, RHR 47-48, no temp elevation) all still look good despite the short-sleep stretch — no signs of digging a hole.

Quality days stay genuinely hard when they happen: Aug 4's threshold session put over 40 of 62 minutes in Z3-Z5 combined with real Z4/Z5 time — the intensity side of polarized training is real, it's the easy side that still needs work.

ACWR has stayed in a safe range through a very up-and-down stretch (0.8 optimal two weeks ago, now 0.2 low) — the body absorbs whatever load shows up, which is exactly what you want heading into an unpredictable newborn phase.
Fitness age is holding at a strong 28.2 (7.8 years under chronological age) straight through the light week — the aerobic base built over the summer isn't going anywhere in a week off.
